title: Precision sensitivity sweep: INT8/GPTQ/mixed kernels (notes & microbench)
body:
TL;DR: Ran a targeted sensitivity sweep across INT8, GPTQ (8bit grouped), and mixed FP8/INT8 fallbacks using three kernel backends (cuBLASLt GEMM, custom int8-fused Triton kernels, and a lightweight CPU fallback). Results show that model-level quality drops (measured via logprob delta + downstream exact-match) are highly non-uniform across layers: embedding and first ~4 transformer blocks are extremely sensitive to aggressive quant, while middle blocks tolerate per-channel 8-bit with negligible quality loss. Kernel choice matters most for latency at sequence lengths >512; cuBLASLt wins for long dense matmuls, Triton-fused wins for smaller matmuls and attention KV cache workloads. Key actionable: enable per-layer quant rules (pin first n blocks to FP16) and prefer Triton-fused int8 kernels for low-latency interactive workloads, fall back to cuBLASLt for batch scoring.

Goals:
- Characterize perf vs quality tradeoffs for INT8, GPTQ (8-bit grouped), and mixed FP8/INT8 configurations.
- Microbenchmark kernel latency and memory footprint for attention and FFN matmuls.
- Produce practical rules for runtime routing and default quant profiles.

Testbed (quick spec):
- HW: p4d.24xlarge (A100 40GB) and g5.12xlarge (A10G) for comparative perf; small CPU fallback on c6i.8x for latency baseline.
- Runtime: serving-runtime branch quant-sweep-2025 (PR 1284), CUDA 12.1, cuBLASLt 12.1, Triton 2.29, custom int8 kernel v0.7.
- Models: Llama-2-13B (hf converted), internal-repro-3B (encoder-decoder toy), BLOOM-3B for odd-activation cases.
- Datasets: wikitext-103 eval (lm logprob), 200-shot QA subset for EM/ROUGE.

Sweep dimensions (what we actually ran):
- Quant types: per-channel INT8 symmetric, GPTQ 8-bit grouped (group=128), AWQ-inspired float8-mixed fallback (FP8 for sensitive layers), FP16 baseline.
- Kernel backends: cuBLASLt GEMM w/auto-tuning, Triton fused int8 kernels (vec4 packing where possible), custom CUDA FP8 kernels (experimental), CPU int8 fallback.
- Sequence lengths: 32, 128, 512, 1024.
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16.

Commands & profiling notes (repro):
- End-to-end: ./run_inference_bench --model llm-13b --quant-config configs/llm-13b/int8-perlayer.json --backend triton --seq 128 --batch 1 --profile
- Kernel microbench: python tools/kernel_microbench.py --kernel triton_int8 --matmul 4096 4096 --repeat 100
- NVTX regions were added around attention forward/backward and KV cache lookup. Use nsight or nvprof to inspect.
- Profiling tip: for int8 fused kernels, counter "gpu_achieved_occupancy" is often useless; watch DRAM throughput and L2 hit rate instead.

High-level observations:
- Quality:
  - INT8 per-channel symmetric: average ll delta +0.7 across wikitext (worse on BLOOM activations), EM drop ~2.5% on QA for full int8.
  - GPTQ 8-bit grouped (group=128): ll delta +0.15, EM drop ~0.4% when group size tuned; group size 256 slightly worse for some runs.
  - FP8-mixed (AWQ style): if we reserve embeddings + first 4 blocks for FP16, overall ll delta +0.08 and EM drop ~0.2% — best quality/cost sweet spot observed.
- Performance:
  - At seq<=128, Triton-fused int8 kernels reduce end-to-end p95 latency by ~22% vs cuBLASLt with INT8 packing overhead.
  - At seq>=512 cuBLASLt autotuned GEMM eclipses Triton for throughput (more efficient larger tile sizes).
  - FP8 kernels are still experimental: memory bandwidth limited on A10G, A100 shows modest wins when fused attention kernels used.
- Memory:
  - Per-layer INT8 reduces activation + weight footprint by ~48% vs FP16; enabling KV cache compression (int8) added ~10% extra improve.

Detailed microbench snippets (representative numbers):
- llm-13b, seq=128, batch=1, A100:
  - FP16 baseline p95: 320ms
  - INT8 (triton fused) p95: 250ms
  - GPTQ (cuBLASLt) p95: 275ms
  - FP8 experimental (triton fused): 238ms but occasional correctness noise (rare token corruptions in 0.02% sequences)
- llm-13b, seq=1024, batch=4, A100:
  - FP16 baseline throughput: 18 tok/s
  - INT8 (cuBLASLt autotuned): 32 tok/s
  - Triton-fused int8: 28 tok/s (kernel overheads add up at large matmul sizes)

Failure modes & gotchas observed:
- Layer normalization folding + int8 scaling subtle bug: per-channel scale rounding caused small distribution shifts; fixed by adding 16-bit accumulator in kernel for LN multiply.
- Token corruption with experimental FP8 kernels traced to underflow in softmax accumulation for long sequences — mitigated by switching attention accumulator to fp16.
- AWQ style heuristics sometimes miss critical early-layer sensitivity when using only weight-hessian proxy; need mixed proxy (activation gradient magnitude + hessian).

Runtime heuristics to implement (recommendations):
- Per-model default: mixed profile: embeddings + first 4 transformer blocks FP16, middle blocks INT8-GPTQ-grouped, last 2 blocks FP16 for safety.
- Kernel routing policy: if seq <= 256 and latency SLO <200ms prefer triton_fused_int8; else prefer cublaslt_int8 for throughput.
- Auto-validate: run quick 100-sample ll delta check during deployment to assert quality within thresholds; auto-fallback to FP16 if delta > 0.5.
- Expose per-layer pins in API: customers can set \"pin_layers\": \"0-3, -2,-1\".

Next experiments (open items):
- Repeat sweep on H100 to check kernel scaling (H100 tensor core behavior may change kernel preference).
- Expand group sizes for GPTQ down to 32 and examine quality/permute artifacts.
- End-to-end cost model: integrate token/sec and spot GPU costs to compute per-1M tokens cost delta for each profile.
- Larger eval sets (squad + code x to check code generation sensitivity).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add a short script to translate AWQ heuristics into per-layer thresholds (see TODO/awq-translate in repo).
- Unify profiler tags with SRE tracing so we can correlate cloud metrics with kernel hotspots.
- Share these draft results with solutions-eng and product-hosted-api for rollout constraints.

Appendix (quick links/commands):
- microbench script: tools/kernel_microbench.py
- reprod runs: s3://redwood-bench/quant/nov2025/run-47/ (contains nvprof traces)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1284

Footnotes: this doc is raw notes from the sweep, contains partial runs and a few diverging configs. Numbers are representative; final release requires deterministic runs and seed control.
